identity.title: Influence Functions for Scalable Data Attribution in Diffusion Models

problem.claim: The paper addresses data attribution and interpretability challenges in diffusion models.

contributions.claim: Extends influence functions to predict changes in diffusion-model generation probabilities using proxy measurements.
Provides a formulation in which prior attribution methods correspond to different design choices.
Uses a diffusion-model-tailored K-FAC approximation based on generalised Gauss–Newton matrices for Hessian computations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by formulating influence functions for generation-probability-related quantities in diffusion models and tailoring scalable Hessian approximation to this setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their recommended method outperforms previously proposed attribution methods on LDS and retraining without top influences, without method-specific hyperparameter tuning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion models advance generative modelling, while adoption creates data-attribution and interpretability challenges.
The paper extends influence functions from supervised-loss changes to changes in the probability of generating a particular example, measured through proxies.
It formulates these quantities, interprets prior methods as design choices, and introduces a diffusion-tailored K-FAC approximation for scalable Hessian computation.
The authors report stronger performance on LDS and retraining-without-top-influences evaluations without method-specific tuning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a target quantity—generation probability—to proxy measurements, then explicitly formulates influence functions for those quantities.

lessons.interpretation: Making the attribution target explicit can clarify what an influence estimate is intended to approximate.
lessons.application: Define the downstream quantity of interest first, list its measurable proxies, and state how each proxy enters the attribution formulation.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the target quantity has no defensible proxy or when proxy choice is itself the central unresolved question.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the proxy measurements, datasets, numerical results, or evaluation protocols.
The magnitude and statistical reliability of the reported performance advantage are not given.
The abstract does not establish priority or independently verify the claimed scalability or performance.
